task_instance: Given a sample multi-channel ad campaign CSV export (Google Search, Google Display, Meta, LinkedIn campaigns with impressions/clicks/conversions/spend/revenue for Aug 2026), perform the skill's full workflow: normalize the data, compute per-campaign and per-channel metrics (CTR, CPC, conv rate, CPA, ROAS), detect budget waste (high-CPA outliers), identify winners, run a statistical-significance check between two Meta campaigns, rank channel efficiency, and produce a budget reallocation plan, delivered as campaign-analysis-2026-09-27.md in the skill's specified output format.
evidence: Created campaign_data.csv (7 campaigns across Google Search, Google Display, Meta, LinkedIn) as sample input data. Wrote analyze.py to compute all normalized metrics (CTR/CPC/ConvRate/CPA/ROAS) per campaign and per channel rollup, spend/conversion shares, an efficiency index, a high-CPA outlier detector (>3x average finite CPA -> flagged LinkedIn InMail at $466.67 CPA), and a two-proportion z-test for statistical significance between Meta Retargeting (7.78% conv rate, n=1800) and Meta Prospecting (2.31% conv rate, n=2250), yielding z=8.13, p<0.0001 (significant). Ran `python3 analyze.py` and captured its output. Used those verified numbers (not fabricated) to write campaign-analysis-2026-09-27.md following the skill's Phase 5 output template: Executive Summary, Performance Dashboard, Budget Waste Report, Winners to Scale, A/B Test Results, Budget Reallocation (efficiency ranking, current-vs-recommended allocation table, funnel stage coverage), and Action Plan. This is a pure-reasoning/calculation skill (per SKILL.md 'Tools Required: No external tools needed') with no bundled scripts, external services, or credentials required, so the full deliverable was produced and verified end-to-end within the sandbox. Verified by re-reading the generated file (123 lines) and cross-checking its tables' numbers against analyze.py's printed output. Files: /tmp/.../exec_gr/github__awesome-copilot__ad-campaign-analyzer@developer-sandbox/{campaign_data.csv, analyze.py, campaign-analysis-2026-09-27.md, result.json}.
